key_insight: Bitumen liberation is shear-driven: detachment occurs only above a critical surface shear stress and increases with higher particle Reynolds number and smaller lump diameter.
engineering_relevance: A shear-based liberation model could guide oil sands hydrotransport operating conditions to improve bitumen recovery.
method: 3D Eulerian–Eulerian CFD with k–omega SST turbulence closure.
Six cases spanning lump diameters of 4–5 cm and particle Reynolds numbers of 2000–4000.
Semi-empirical liberation model based on local shear-driven detachment.
evidence_signal: The proposed model was validated against experimental liberation data, with reported error below 8.3%.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy beyond the studied lump sizes and Reynolds numbers remains unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Numerical Investigations on Bitumen Liberation from Oil Sands Lump
